name: Suspense Engine
prompt: Suspense-first structure: reveal the hidden danger to the viewer early, then let ordinary scenes play while a visible clock counts down. Use POV-object-reaction triplets. Make the key object huge in frame. Angles: high overhead god's-eye, low staircase angles, tight insert close-ups. Camera: slow deliberate push-ins, occasional vertigo dolly-zoom on revelation. Lighting: high-contrast 1950s Technicolor or black-and-white noir, hard key light, long shadows, saturated reds and greens. Music: nervous repeating strings, sudden silence before the reveal. Shot length 4-7 s, tightening to 2 s at the climax.
translatable: tell the audience the danger early, ticking clock, big inserts of the important object, high overhead angles, POV → object → reaction triads, slow push-in, dolly-zoom (animated clip), stalking string ostinato. Not translatable: actor menace, cameo.
shots: (a) Overhead god's-eye view of an office at 11:58 PM, 31 Dec 1999, one beige PC glowing; slow push-in, 6 s. (b) Extreme insert of a wall clock's second hand, then an insert of a two-digit "99" year field on a green screen; 2 s each. (c) Reaction: a sysadmin's eyes in a hard key light, reflected digits rolling to "00"; music cuts to silence, 3 s.
topics: hoaxes with a "hidden bomb" (scams, fake deadlines, doomsday predictions), viral rumors with a reveal.

name: Cold Symmetry
prompt: Perfectly centered one-point perspective, vanishing point dead center, corridors and rooms receding. Ultra-wide 18mm lens, deep focus, cold clinical white, sterile red, or candlelit painterly tableaux. Camera: slow, steady forward track or locked-off static; never handheld. Character stares up from under a lowered brow toward the lens. Bold sans-serif title cards announce chapters (e.g., 'DECEMBER 31'). Music: grand classical waltz or eerie choral drones set against mundane images. Long shots, 8-12 s.
translatable: one-point-perspective corridors, symmetry, slow forward tracks, wide lens, clinical white or red sets, chapter cards, classical music used ironically, the stare (risky with AI). ASL about 11 s. Not translatable: obsessive performance takes.
shots: (a) One-point corridor of identical server racks, a lone figure at the vanishing point; slow forward track, 12 s. (b) Title card, white sans-serif on black: "THE LAST NIGHT OF THE CENTURY", 3 s. (c) A mainframe's red indicator light fills a cold white room, symmetrical; a waltz plays over the silence, 10 s.
topics: technology panic, AI fears, science-gone-wrong myths, bureaucracy.

name: Weather & Crowds
prompt: Every frame contains moving weather: driving rain, wind-whipped banners, drifting smoke, falling snow. Crowds clump together or scatter as one body. Long telephoto lens compressing many figures into layered depth. Each character has one exaggerated signature gesture. Camera moves have a clear start, middle, and end; cut on motion. Transitions: hard horizontal wipe. Palette: monochrome silver or muted earth with one bold color. Music: sparse taiko drums, wind sound. Shots 3-6 s.
translatable: weather in every shot (rain, wind, snow, smoke), crowds that gather or scatter, one gesture per character, camera moves with a beginning, middle and end, cut on motion, wipe transitions, telephoto compression. Not translatable: choreographed actor movement (only partly, via animated clips).
shots: (a) Telephoto view of a crowd in snowy Times Square, breath steam and confetti drifting, 5 s. (b) Wipe to a rain-streaked window: IT staff huddle around one terminal, then split into pairs; lateral track, 6 s. (c) A banner reading "Y2K READY" whips in the wind; cut on its motion to Owlbert's feathers ruffling, 3 s.
topics: mass panic, moral panics, crowd behavior, bank runs.

name: Newsreel & Shadows
prompt: Open with a scratchy black-and-white newsreel that reveals the ending, so the story asks WHY. Retell events through several conflicting witnesses. Deep focus: foreground face and distant background both sharp. Low angles showing ceilings; chiaroscuro hard light, German-expressionist shadows. Transitions: long dissolves. Use one-set montage to compress years. Short 5-15 s musical bridges with recurring motifs. Narrator acts as a playful magician exposing a trick. Shots 4-8 s.
translatable: a fake newsreel cold open that gives away the outcome, multiple narrators re-telling events, deep focus with foreground and background both sharp, low angles with ceilings, chiaroscuro, long dissolves, a time-compression montage on one set, short 5-15 s music bridge cues with leitmotifs, and a magician-narrator framing ("I'm going to show you a trick"). Not translatable: Welles's voice and presence (Owlbert takes that role).
shots: (a) Grainy newsreel title "NEWS OF THE MILLENNIUM: THE BUG THAT WASN'T" over planes landing safely, 6 s. (b) Low angle: a programmer in the foreground, with the ceiling and a wall calendar showing "1999" sharp in the deep background, 7 s. (c) Montage: the same kitchen table in 1972, 1985 and 1998; the two-digit date on a printout never changes; long dissolves, 4 s each.
topics: forgery and fakes, biography of a hoaxer, "how a myth was built."

name: Showdown Wides & Eyes
prompt: Alternate vast panoramic widescreen landscapes with extreme close-ups of eyes, hands, and objects. Long silence, then a single whistled or harmonica-like motif. Frame a ritual standoff: two sides facing each other across an empty space. Cross-cut between them, each shot shorter than the last (6 s → 1 s). Palette: sun-bleached ochre, dust haze, deep shadow under hat brims. Camera: slow push into the eyes; static wides. Music swells only at the decisive moment.
translatable: extreme close-ups next to vast wide shots, long silences, ritual standoffs, music as a character, rhythmic cross-cutting that speeds up. Not translatable: drawn-out actor stares across many minutes (it needs compressing for YouTube).
shots: (a) Panoramic wide: a lone desktop PC on a desk in an empty open-plan office stretching to the horizon, 7 s. (b) Extreme close-up of the clock reading 11:59, then of the monitor's blinking cursor; cross-cut that speeds up, 2→1 s. (c) Showdown title card: "THE CLAIM" on one side, "THE EVIDENCE" on the other; whistled motif, 5 s.
topics: claim versus evidence face-offs, famous debates, viral feuds.

name: Confession Noir
prompt: Narrator confesses up front how it ended, then rewinds. Camera stays unobtrusive: eye-level medium shots, simple cuts, no flourish. Black-and-white film noir lighting, venetian-blind shadow stripes, cigarette-smoke haze, 1940s offices. Plant small props early that pay off later. Wry ironic cuts that undercut a claim. Music: muted brass, sparse jazz. Shots 5-8 s.
translatable: a narrator who already knows the outcome, venetian-blind noir light, setups and payoffs, a mostly unobtrusive camera, witty title-cut juxtapositions. Not translatable: dialogue performance.
shots: (a) Noir office, blind-stripe shadows across a ledger: "They said the planes would fall. Here's how they didn't," 7 s. (b) Plant: a sticky note reading "FIX DATES" on a monitor in 1997, 4 s. (c) Payoff: the same faded note on a working terminal, 1 Jan 2000, 5 s.
topics: scams, fraud stories, "who profited from the panic."

name: Wonder Push-In
prompt: Build wonder: slow push-in on an upturned awed face lit by a light offscreen; delay revealing the source. Backlit volumetric god-rays, gentle lens flare, warm suburban dusk or night blue. Child's-eye low angle. Long fluid camera moves that travel across one big scene to reframe several subjects in a single shot. Music: soaring orchestral theme with a hummable motif, swelling at reveals. Shots 4-8 s; occasional 12-15 s travelling shot.
translatable: slow push-in on an awed face looking offscreen, delayed reveal of the thing, shafts of backlight, a child's-eye low angle, a heroic orchestral motif. The "oner" partly carries over as a long multi-stage camera move across one large still. Not translatable: actor restaging in a real long take.
shots: (a) A kid in pajamas, face lit blue by a TV countdown, slow push-in, 6 s. (b) Reveal: city skyline fireworks; the lights stay on; volumetric rays, 7 s. (c) One long move across a family living room from parents to a dog to a VCR clock blinking "12:00", 12 s.
topics: science wins, "the experts fixed it," hopeful, family-friendly.

name: Dollhouse Symmetry
prompt: Perfectly symmetrical, centered, flat straight-on compositions like a dollhouse diorama; subject dead center, rule of thirds ignored. Wide lens, deep focus, slight fisheye. Saturated pastel palette (powder pink, mustard yellow, mint, baby blue) consistent across set and costume. Bright soft even lighting, even at night. Overhead top-down inserts of tidy objects. Camera: locked-off; whip pans 90°; lateral dolly past cutaway rooms. Chapter title cards in clean geometric sans-serif. Music: harpsichord, plucked strings, glockenspiel. Shots 3-5 s.
translatable: dead-center symmetry, flat straight-on frames, pastel palettes kept consistent in each frame, overhead inserts, whip pans, lateral tracks past cutaway sets, chapter cards, deadpan narrator. Not translatable: deadpan ensemble acting (partly via expressions).
shots: (a) Centered pastel-mint server room, a technician in a mustard cardigan facing the lens, 4 s. (b) Overhead insert: a neatly arranged floppy disk, a manual and a pencil on a pink desk, 3 s. (c) Lateral track past a cutaway building: four rooms, four people checking four clocks; card: "CHAPTER 2: THE PATCH", 6 s.
topics: lighthearted myth explainers, quirky history, lists of hoaxes.

name: Timeline Collision
prompt: Interleave two or three timelines (years, hours, minutes) with on-screen time stamps, cross-cutting faster as they converge on one moment. Monumental wide establishing shots against tight tactile inserts. Palette: steel blue, charcoal, sodium orange, natural daylight; large-format film grain, high clarity. Camera: steady push-ins, aerial wides. Music: relentless ticking pulse rising in pitch; drop to silence at convergence. Shots 2-4 s, 6 s for wides.
translatable: interlocking timelines, cross-cutting to a convergence, a ticking score, ASL about 3 s, huge wides against tight inserts, cool palette. Not translatable: practical effects, IMAX film texture.
shots: (a) Card "1970 – THE SHORTCUT": a coder writes "YY" on punch-card forms, 3 s. (b) Card "1998 – THE AUDIT", a team reviewing printouts; cross-cut with (a), 3 s. (c) Card "00:00:00 – THE MOMENT": an aerial wide of a city grid staying lit; the ticking stops, 5 s.
topics: how a rumor mutated over time, cause-and-effect chains, timelines.

name: Forensic Cool
prompt: Clinical, omniscient camera: locked-off or precise smooth moves synced to subject motion, never wobbly (one handheld shot max per video, for a single panicked POV). Desaturated low-key grade, sickly fluorescent green and sodium yellow, deep shadow. Close-ups only for decisive evidence: documents, screens, timestamps. Procedural insert montages of files and data. Music: low ambient electronic drones, muted pulses. Shots 3-5 s.
translatable: a locked-off omniscient camera, moves timed exactly to the subject's motion, rare handheld (once), close-ups saved for key evidence, desaturated grade with sickly green or yellow accents, procedural inserts of screens and documents, ambient electronic score. Not translatable: dozens of takes, micro-performance.
shots: (a) Locked-off, desaturated green: a 1999 cubicle farm at night, one monitor lit, 5 s. (b) Insert close-up: COBOL code with "IF YR < 50" highlighted, 3 s. (c) Precise slow pan across a corkboard of news clippings saying "TEOTWAWKI", ending on a memo marked "REMEDIATED", 5 s.
topics: investigative debunks, scams, data forensics, tracking a fake's origin.

name: Rise, Fall & Freeze
prompt: Rise-and-fall arc narrated in voiceover; freeze-frame at key moments while narrator comments. Energetic crash zooms and whip pans in the rise; long, quiet held shots in the fall. Slow-motion close-ups on faces. Warm tungsten, smoky saturated reds and golds; later cooler and greyer. Music: period pop/rock needle drops on the rise, then sudden silence. Shots 2-4 s rising, 6-10 s falling.
translatable: freeze frames with narrator commentary, more than one narrator, rise-and-fall arc, needle-drop music, whip pans and crash zooms, slow-motion faces, strategic silence. ASL about 7 s (*The Irishman*). Not translatable: Steadicam long takes, actor improvisation.
shots: (a) A crash zoom onto a 1998 survivalist-store owner beside stacked canned goods; freeze frame plus narrator line, 3 s. (b) Montage of Y2K-kit infomercials, whip-pan cuts with a period dance track, 2 s each. (c) January 2000: the same store, empty and grey, held silently, 9 s.
topics: grifters who cashed in on panic, the rise and fall of misinformation influencers.

name: Breathing Room
prompt: Hand-painted watercolor-and-gouache anime look, lush greens, towering cumulus clouds, warm afternoon light. After each idea, insert a quiet pause shot: a character simply sits, wind moves grass, water flows, steam rises from tea. Gentle lateral drifts and slow tilts up to the sky. No villains; misunderstandings are human and forgivable. Music: soft piano and strings, often silent with ambient nature sound. Shots 5-9 s; pauses 4-6 s.
translatable: "ma" pauses (characters sit, sigh, nothing happens), nature and sky, wind, food, flight, gentle piano and orchestral themes, no villain. Not translatable: hand-drawn character animation, but painterly AI stills suit it well.
shots: (a) A countryside village on New Year's Eve, painted sky, a slow tilt up to the stars, 8 s. (b) Pause: a grandmother sips tea beside an old radio, steam rising; no narration, 5 s. (c) Owlbert perched on a windmill as dawn breaks and the lights stay on; wind ruffles feathers, 6 s.
topics: nature and environment myths, kid-friendly episodes, gentle "nobody's evil, people just misunderstood."

name: Archive Pan
prompt: Documentary of still images: period photographs and documents animated with slow zooms, gentle pans, and 2.5D parallax. Start tight on one face, pull out to reveal the wider group. Slow crossfades. Sepia, faded Kodachrome, or newsprint grain matching the era. Quotations from period documents read aloud while the camera drifts across the paper. Music: solo fiddle, piano, or acoustic guitar, sparse and elegiac. Shots 6-12 s.
translatable: slow zooms and pans over stills, parallax, a zoom out from one person to reveal others, fades, readings of period documents, sparse period music. This is the pipeline's native mode, since it is exactly "stills with camera moves". Not translatable: real archives (AI stills must be labeled as illustrations, not archival photos, to avoid creating fake history; see Q3).
shots: (a) Sepia-style illustration of a 1960s computer room; slow zoom into one operator's hands on a punch card, 10 s. (b) Pan across an illustrated 1999 memo while its text is read aloud, 9 s. (c) Start on one engineer's tired smile, pull out to reveal a room of 40 colleagues, 12 s.
topics: historical propaganda, long-form history debunks, wartime myths.

name: Contested Reenactment
prompt: Investigate how people came to believe something false. Narrator looks straight into the lens, centered, plain dark background, soft key light. Replay each competing version of an event as a stylized slow-motion reenactment, isolating single objects in extreme close-up against black. Archival documents and headlines in macro detail. Restate the claim, then the contradiction. Music: hypnotic minimalist repeating arpeggios, cyclical and unresolved. Shots 4-8 s.
translatable: the subject speaks straight into the lens (Owlbert as Interrotron host), stylized slow-motion reenactments of each *version* of events, extreme close-ups of documents and objects, a minimalist repeating score, focus on how belief went wrong. Not translatable: real interviews.
shots: (a) Owlbert dead center against a dark backdrop, eyes to the lens: "What did people think would happen?", 6 s. (b) Version A reenactment: an elevator cable snaps in slow motion, stylized and red-lit; label "THE RUMOR", 5 s. (c) Version B: the same elevator doors simply open at 12:01; label "THE RECORD"; macro insert of a maintenance log, 5 s.
topics: the channel's core format. How a false story spread, witness confusion, wrongful accusations.

name: Curious Collage
prompt: Playful personal essay: the host appears on screen exploring, holding photographs, framing things with hands. Mix still photographs, collage cut-outs, and moving shots; photos within frames. Everyday people and ordinary objects treated with affection and curiosity. Episodic chapters with handwritten intertitles; an on-screen clock may track time. Bright natural daylight, French new-wave black-and-white or sunny pastel color. Music: light chanson, whimsical woodwinds. Shots 4-7 s.
translatable: the host on screen as a curious self-portrait, photos inside film and film inside photos, documentary and fiction mixed, ordinary people, a near-real-time clock structure, episodic chapters, gentle humor. Not translatable: real street encounters.
shots: (a) Owlbert holds up an instant photo of a 1999 family stockpiling water; the photo "comes alive", 6 s. (b) Collage of cut-out newspaper headlines pinned on a laundry line, wind moving them, 5 s. (c) Handwritten intertitle "11:47 PM — Still nothing", then a baker kneading dough, unbothered, 5 s.
topics: everyday myths, personal-scale misinformation (health tips, family WhatsApp rumors).

name: Kinetic Montage
prompt: Rapid-fire comedic montage: extreme close-up inserts of mundane actions (button press, mug slam, floppy insert), each cut on a music beat with a punchy sound effect. Whip-pan transitions between locations. Gags happen in frame: something enters from edge, background detail pays off. Saturated punchy color, crisp lighting. Repeat a visual motif three times with escalating variation. Music: upbeat retro rock/funk, edits locked to the beat. Shots 0.5-2 s in montages, 3-4 s otherwise.
translatable: hyper-montage of close-ups of small actions with matching sound effects, whip-pan transitions, cuts on the beat, visual gags inside the frame. Not translatable: comic timing of actors; it partly carries over through quick cuts and Owlbert's animated reactions.
shots: (a) Hyper-montage: a finger presses "SAVE", a floppy clicks in, a mug slams down, the clock flips; four beats, 0.5 s each. (b) A whip pan from a newscaster yelling "CHAOS!" to a sleepy man in a dressing gown placidly feeding a cat, 3 s. (c) The third repeat of the motif: the same mug-slam insert, now with Owlbert's wing knocking it over, 1.5 s.
topics: listicle debunks, fast "top 5 myths", comedic shorts; not tragic topics.

name: Class Geography
prompt: Stage meaning in space: haves high and lit, have-nots low and shadowed; stairs and basements; left-to-right progress versus right-to-left retreat. Telephoto side-profile shots that flatten figures against backgrounds. Ensemble frames where several people react in one composition. Windows and doorways as frames within frames. Tone may swerve from comedy to unease. Naturalistic Korean-thriller grade: cool greens, warm interior pools. Music: baroque-tinged strings, ironic elegance. Shots 4-7 s.
translatable: telephoto profile shots, ensemble staging with many people in one frame, screen direction carrying meaning (left/right, up/down), vertical class geography (stairs, basements), sharp tonal swerves, frames within frames. Not translatable: ensemble acting.
shots: (a) Vertical split: executives in a bright penthouse toasting "Y2K compliant" while a basement IT crew below works by desk lamp, 6 s. (b) Telephoto profile: a consultant walking left-to-right past a line of worried clerks, 5 s. (c) A window frame within the frame: a family glimpsed through a window, counting canned food, 5 s.
topics: who profits from misinformation, class and inequality myths, satire.

name: Direct Address Heat
prompt: Characters face the lens head-on, one after another, each stating a belief (rapid direct-address montage). Floating dolly effect: subject stays fixed while background glides behind, as if carried toward camera. Dutch tilted angles for tension. Hot saturated palette: crimson, amber, deep orange, humid light. Intercut archival-style inserts. Bold block-letter title cards. Music: jazz horns, soulful brass, protest-song energy. Shots 2-4 s in address montage, 5-7 s otherwise.
translatable: a rapid series of people addressing the lens, the double-dolly float (subject and background drifting, done with a parallax cut-out), Dutch angles, saturated heat palette, archival-style inserts cut into the story, jazz scoring. Not translatable: real actors; sensitive topics need extra care.
shots: (a) A direct-address montage of five neighbors, each facing the lens: "The banks will crash," "My VCR will explode," and so on, 2 s each. (b) Float shot: a sysadmin glides toward the camera while the server hall slides past behind them, 5 s. (c) A Dutch-angle insert of a 1999 tabloid headline, then a bold title card "WAKE UP", 3 s.
topics: civic and history misinformation, community rumor dynamics. Use with care on race-related topics.
